summary: Opaque 503s from compression-queue saturation and retry amplification during high webhook ingestion
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reported a sudden increase in 503 responses from our hosted API for BrightNote Health during a high-volume webhook ingestion window. Errors surfaced at ~2026-03-11T18:02Z and persisted for ~18 minutes. Responses were opaque 503s from API gateway with upstream runtime timeouts. Impact:
- BrightNote observed ~45% error rate on ingestion webhook endpoints (affects production ML feature ingestion and downstream user-facing alerts).
- Customer has enterprise SLA; revenue-impacting.
Environment:
- prod/us-east-1, dedicated customer shard (tenant: brightnote-prod), model variants: open/llama-2-13b (inference), embed/fast-encoder-v1 (embeddings).
- Recent runtime hotpatch deployed to ingress-compressor for a compression worker priority fix (hotpatch ID: HP-2026-03-10-4).
Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Send 10k small webhook messages in steady burst (payloads ~1-2KB) with client retries (retry policy jittered).
2) API gateway begins to queue and hand off to ingress-compressor which batches/compresses payloads before runtime fanout.
3) After sustained rate, compression queue depth climbs, compressor workers hit CPU saturation, handoffs to runtime begin to stall.
4) Upstream runtime connections time out; API gateway surfaces 503s.
Logs and telemetry pointers are below.
steps_to_reproduce: Trigger a webhook burst: 10k requests over 2 minutes to /v1/webhook/ingest with Content-Type: application/json
Ensure client retry behavior is enabled (exponential backoff with jitter).
Observe ingress-compressor queue depth and compressor CPU on prod shard brightnote-prod.
Watch for API gateway 5xx counters and upstream runtime timeouts in Grafana dashboards.
logs: 2026-03-11T18:02:09Z APIGW [tenant=brightnote-prod] upstream request timed out after 8s -> 503
2026-03-11T18:05:10Z COMPRESSOR hotpatch HP-2026-03-10-4 applied -> increased worker-priority scheduling observed
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: the hotpatch to ingress-compressor changed internal worker scheduling priorities which, under sustained webhook retry traffic, allowed compression queue to grow and compression workers to monopolize CPU. This caused handoff latency to serving-runtime and a cascade of upstream timeouts from the API gateway. Key findings:
- Compressor queue depth (graph: grafana/dashboard/ingress-compressor?q=brightnote-prod) rose linearly from ~50 to >1800 during the 18-minute window.
- Compressor worker CPU hit 95-99% on 4/4 workers; syscalls and context switch rate increased (node exporter: high softirq).
- API gateway timed-out upstream connections after configured 8s; concurrent hedged retries from client amplified load (retry loops visible in access logs).
- Heap/stack traces from one runtime instance show long GC pauses but not the root cause; CPU was dominated by compressor processes on ingress nodes.
- No network packet loss or disk iowait spike detected.
Correlated items: HP-2026-03-10-4 (hotpatch) deployed ~3 hours before the event and changed compressor scheduling; rollback candidate.
resolution:
Immediate actions taken:
- Rolled back hotpatch HP-2026-03-10-4 at 2026-03-11T18:12Z; compressor worker scheduling reverted.
- Scaled ingress-compressor workers from 4 -> 8 on brightnote-prod shard and applied temporary CPU limits to compressor process to prevent monopolization.
- Applied short-term rate-limiting on webhook ingress for tenant brightnote-prod to 2000 rps with a 30s token bucket to allow queues to drain.
- Coordinated with customer to throttle client retry policy (recommended max 3 retries with exponential backoff min 250ms).
Outcome: error rate dropped to baseline within 5 minutes after rollback and scaling. Postmortem follow-ups scheduled.
Permanent follow-ups (action items):
- Rework compressor hotpatch with better scheduler testing and canary (OWNER: infra-rt).
- Add direct compression-queue depth alert with auto-scale playbook.
- Harden ingress hedged-retry protections to detect and cut amplification loops.
- Add e2e load tests for webhook + compression path in staging.
